method: Complete reads of twelve pinned source files; verified Git blobs and SHA256. Executed original verify.py in separate Python processes with synthetic reports and temporary authored files. Build and cache-dropping scripts only read, not executed.
findings: verify.py groups report rows by checksum and compares independently computed SHA1 values within each group. It does not derive expected groups from input roots, check omitted files, verify checksum labels against a declared algorithm or ensure group cardinality.

Executed control shows equal pair accepted and unequal pair under one label rejected. Equal files assigned distinct labels and report with no body are also accepted: this checker cannot establish recall/completeness.

bisect.sh runs one timed command, attempts Linux cache dropping and warns but continues on failure. It does not separately require successful rmlint exit before classifying runtime; string manipulation assumes time output can become integer centiseconds. No pairing, confidence interval or correctness gate is provided here.

Baseline hashes regular-file paths with MD5, skips empty files, follows os.path.isfile symlinks, stores global digest groups and returns only aggregate duplicate/group counts. Errors return no digest. This differs from byte-confirmed equality and physical-alias handling in our library.

Several build scripts clone moving branches without a commit pin; release scripts select tags but do not verify binary hashes. rdfind script downloads an old version over HTTP without a content hash. These historical scripts do not establish a reproducible current benchmark environment.
copytodocs copies matching plot files into fixed documentation names without validating provenance or benchmark semantics.
